tool_args.rationale: The five baseline rows identify a saturating term plus a square-root term to rounding precision. The two off-baseline rows change drive and sink gradient together, leaving the sink coupling unresolved. Use the trajectory batch to test how the response changes with drive away from the baseline gradient before spending a confirmation.

considered_alternatives.option: Confirm a two-term law with sink dependence only in the saturation denominator
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: It fits all seven observations to rounding precision, but the data do not distinguish it from a law in which the sink also changes the square-root contribution.

considered_alternatives.option: Confirm a two-term law with sink dependence in both contributions
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: It fits equally well, yet at u_now=0.5 and s_grad=0.2 the two laws predict about 2.97 and 2.83, respectively, a gap larger than the 0.045 tolerance.
The first acquisition established sink inhibition, but sampled only one drive level at each off-baseline gradient. Repeating those conditions would not separate the two effects.
